chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and Murazim, and Shu'ayb, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:
Regarding a man performing tamattu' who enters on the night of 'Arafah: he performs tawaf and sa'y, then exits ihram, then enters ihram again, and comes to Mina. He said: There is no harm in that.

key_terms.فَيَطُوفُ: he performs tawaf around the Ka'bah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ: the night before the standing of 'Arafah
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, the sacred site to which pilgrims proceed during hajj
key_terms.وَيَسْعَى: he performs sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah
key_terms.يُحِلُّ: he exits the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim performing tamattu' who arrives on the night of 'Arafah still complete the rites and proceed to Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one performing hajj al-tamattu' who arrives on the night of 'Arafah. It indicates that he may perform tawaf and sa'y, exit ihram, then enter ihram again and proceed to Mina, and that there is no problem in doing so.
